---
title: "How it works"
---

The site is rendered from the [`fhperf`](https://github.com/ThomUK/synthetic-hospital-performance)
R package. Everything a metric needs is in three folders under `inst/`.

## Ids and domains

Every id is `<domain>_<nnn>`, for example `ed_003`. The domain codes are
listed in `inst/domains.yaml`, each naming the subject matter expert group
expected to own its definitions: `ed`, `apc`, `op`, `rtt` and `diag` so
far. Metrics and components share one numbering within a domain, and a new
id is simply the next free number under the owning domain. The validator
rejects any id whose domain is not in the list.

A count is one id. Its metric file omits `numerator`, and the component
with the same id supplies the events. Anything with a denominator is three
ids: the metric, its numerator and its denominator, each defined once and
reusable, so `ed_003` (four-hour performance) is `ed_002 / ed_001` and
`diag_002` (imaging requests per 1,000 attendances) reuses `ed_001` as its
denominator. The [index](catalogue.qmd) lists them all.

## Components

A **component** is one YAML file in `inst/components/` and one SQL file in
`inst/sql/`, sharing an id. The SQL returns **one row per event** with an
`event_date` column and, if the component sums rather than counts, a
numeric `value` column. The YAML says which it does:

```yaml
id: apc_003
title: Inpatient bed-minutes
aggregate: sum
unit: minutes
source: derived.spells
```

Components are the numerators and denominators. They have their own ids
because denominators are reused: `ed_001` is the denominator of the
four-hour performance and of imaging requests per 1,000 attendances, and
also the ED attendance count metric itself.

Snapshot components, such as the RTT waiting list at each month end, write
`{{window_start}}` and `{{window_end}}` in their SQL and the package fills
them in as `DATE` literals.

## Metrics

A **metric** is one YAML file in `inst/metrics/`. It names its numerator,
its denominator unless it is a count, and how to combine them:

```yaml
id: apc_004
title: Mean length of stay
type: mean            # count | percentage | rate | mean
numerator: apc_003    # inpatient bed-minutes
denominator: apc_002  # inpatient discharges
divisor: 1440         # minutes to days
unit: days
grain: month          # month | week | day
improvement_direction: decrease
```

For each period the value is `numerator / denominator × multiplier ÷ divisor`.
The multiplier defaults to 100 for a percentage, 1,000 for a rate and 1
otherwise. A period whose denominator is zero has no value. Optional fields
are `target` and `rebase` (a list of dates), which are passed straight to
`NHSRplotthedots::ptd_spc()`.

## The pipeline

1. `read_catalogue()` reads and validates every YAML.
2. `read_component_events()` runs a component's SQL through DBI.
3. `aggregate_events()` counts or sums the events into complete periods.
4. `combine_components()` turns numerator and denominator into a metric series.
5. `metric_spc()` and `plot_metric()` wrap NHSRplotthedots.

`build_metrics()` runs steps 2 to 4 for every metric, reading each component
once. The site's `_build.R` calls it once per render and saves the result;
the pages only read that file.

## The data

The dataset is the Fake NHS Trust's **sample** set, 5% of patients, opened
through the [`fakehospdata`](https://github.com/ThomUK/synthetic-hospital-data/tree/main/fakehospdata)
package as an in-memory DuckDB database. Nothing in it is real.
